stories.label: US Wins Over 23 More Countries in UN Vote Against Cuba Embargo
stories.summary: 130 states again condemned the US embargo on Cuba (34th year), but 17 voted against and 25 abstained — 23 more than last year — after a US campaign of threatened tariffs, visa denials and aid cuts. Lead with who flipped (UAE, Lithuania, Slovenia, Costa Rica, Colombia, Honduras, Chile) and the mechanism of the arm-twisting; then what the embargo does on the island now — the 30% tariff threat on fuel shippers that has deepened Cuba's blackouts and hit hospitals, water and food distribution. Datelined Havana.

stories.label: One hour to leave: Hebron families displaced by Israel’s military operation don’t know when they’ll return
stories.summary: Israeli forces have expelled 407 Palestinian families — nearly 2,650 people — from their homes in Hebron, given one hour and one bag, sealed the city's entrances and closed the Ibrahimi Mosque to Muslim worshippers. Lead with the numbers and the closure of the mosque; name the unit and authority ordering it, and the absence of any return date. Continuation of displacement is the development. Datelined Hebron.

stories.label: Ethiopia Gets 12 Russian Su-35 Fighters, Eyes S-400 Air Defenses
stories.summary: Abiy Ahmed says 12 Russian Su-35 fighters arrived a year early and four S-400 batteries are to follow — making Ethiopia one of the few African air forces with front-line Russian jets. Lead with the deal's size; the stakes are Ethiopia's tensions with Eritrea and Egypt over the Red Sea and the Nile dam, and Russia's widening arms and port reach on Africa's east coast. Datelined Addis Ababa.

stories.label: Um ano após chacina, as crianças da Penha precisam voltar a ser crianças
stories.summary: A year after the Rio police raid on the Penha and Alemão favelas — the deadliest police operation in Brazil's history — the politicians who backed it have just been elected, while children in the communities still live with the trauma. Lead with that contrast: accountability that never came, rewarded at the ballot box. Give the raid's death toll and what investigations found. Datelined Rio de Janeiro.

stories.label: Fed likely to go into wait-and-see mode on rates
stories.summary: The Fed held its rate at 3.75-4% under Chair Kevin Warsh, a month after its first hike in three years, saying more data will guide the next move — the last decision before the US midterms, fought over the cost of living and oil-driven inflation from the Iran war. Lead with the decision and any dissents; name the series: the Fed funds rate, the US 10-year Treasury yield, US inflation. Datelined Washington.

stories.label: Is This What Being "In Hock" Looks Like?: The Readout
stories.summary: Material new development beyond this morning's gas standing-charge story: Chancellor John Healey has now delivered Burnham's first budget, and its frame is the fiscal damage of the Iran war — higher energy costs, weaker growth and borrowing per the OBR. Lead with the headline borrowing and tax numbers and who pays; the mechanism is how a war 5,000km away blew a hole in Britain's public finances. Do not re-lead on standing charges. Datelined London.

stories.label: Why the world's first spinal cord transplant is so controversial | New Scientist
stories.summary: Surgeons in Russia have performed the first spinal cord transplant in people, but the animal and clinical evidence behind it is thin. Lead with what was done and on whom; the mechanism is why spinal tissue rarely reconnects, and the accountability question is consent and evidence standards when a first-in-human operation outruns the data. Datelined Moscow.

stories.label: How Spiders Spin ‘Silk Dope’ Into Nature’s Toughest Material
stories.summary: Biologists probing the molecular structure of spider 'silk dope' are finding how a tangle of unstructured proteins, held as liquid condensates, turns into a thread tougher than steel by weight. Lead with that transformation; the stakes are why decades of synthetic-silk attempts failed and what the mechanism means for materials.

stories.label: Evidence of a spying operation by ICE against left-wing social movements
stories.summary: Wired reports ICE is running one of the largest surveillance operations against left-wing movements in US history — a 'Cointelpro 2.0'. Lead with the scale and the tools (social-media monitoring, data brokers, informants) and who is targeted; the accountability gap is an immigration agency turned domestic political police days before the midterms. 982 points on Hacker News signals reader attention. Datelined Washington.

stories.label: US sanctions Russians, North Koreans for laundering IT worker earnings
stories.summary: The US Treasury sanctioned Russian and North Korean nationals for laundering the pay of North Korean remote IT workers who pose as freelancers at foreign tech firms. Lead with the laundering route through Russia; the mechanism is how hidden remote hires fund Pyongyang's weapons programme, and the Russia–North Korea financial channel the war has deepened. Datelined Pyongyang.

stories.label: Anthropic巨亏背后，藏着行业什么秘密？
stories.summary: TMTPost reads Anthropic's heavy losses as a structural fact of the AI industry: model companies' valuations are parasitic on their infrastructure suppliers — the cloud and chip firms that invest in them and take the money back as compute spend. Lead with the loss figures and the circular-financing mechanism; this is how China's tech press reads the US AI boom. Datelined Beijing.

stories.label: Präsidentschaftswahl in Brasilien: Gewonnen mit und trotz Internet
stories.summary: Lula won re-election despite a Brazilian right that dominates social media, with an online operation led by André Janones that used the networks to drive mobilisation on the ground rather than to win the feed. Lead with that mechanism — how a left campaign beat platform asymmetry — and what it says about elections run on WhatsApp and YouTube. Datelined Brasília.

stories.label: At least 10 dead after two trains collide in Spain
stories.summary: Two high-speed trains collided head-on near Urda, Toledo, killing at least 10, and officials expect the toll to rise. Lead with the toll and the question the reports raise: how two trains on Spain's high-speed network, run by Renfe and Iryo, ended up on the same track, and whether a rail fracture was the cause. Datelined Toledo.

stories.label: 4 Takeaways From Israel's Election
stories.summary: The results are in and neither Netanyahu's bloc (about 53 seats with 85.6% counted, per Middle East Eye) nor Eisenkot's opposition reaches a Knesset majority without the Palestinian parties. Lead with that arithmetic: the only path to a non-Netanyahu government runs through the parties of Israel's Palestinian citizens, whose turnout was historic (New Lines). The structural why: both blocs treat an Arab partner as taboo, so the choice is breaking it or a sixth election in under a decade. Datelined Jerusalem.

stories.label: Oil prices up due to Houthi strikes and US threat to renew Iran war | The National
stories.summary: A Houthi attack on a Saudi Arabian refinery and Washington's threat to resume the war on Iran pushed Brent crude back up, past $116 for the second time in October (Mehr), and UBS now expects Brent near $110 through year-end on falling inventories and record freight costs. Lead with the refinery strike as the cause; the mechanism is supply already squeezed by Hormuz, so each new attack moves the price. Name the series: Brent crude and WTI crude. Datelined where the refinery was hit.

stories.label: Iranians face energy squeeze from war as natural gas runs short
stories.summary: US and Israeli strikes damaged Iran's gas-processing plants, and Tehran is now telling citizens to cut use of heavily subsidised natural gas and civil servants to work from home before winter. Lead with who pays: ordinary households in a country with some of the world's largest gas reserves, facing a heating shortage because the processing, not the gas, was bombed. Name the series: natural gas. Datelined Tehran.

stories.label: John Healey to end standing charges on gas bills for 23m homes
stories.summary: Ahead of his first budget, Chancellor John Healey will ask Ofgem to abolish the fixed daily standing charge on gas bills for 23 million homes from 2027, saving about £45 a year on average. Lead with the mechanism: the standing charge is paid regardless of use, so it falls hardest on low-use, low-income households, and removing it shifts network costs onto the per-unit price. Name the series: natural gas. Datelined London.

stories.label: Adani returns to profit on copper, renewables and airports units
stories.summary: Adani Enterprises broke its streak of quarterly losses in July-September, carried by its copper smelter, renewable-equipment and airports units. Lead with copper: the Kutch smelter turned a profit as copper prices ran high, which shows where India's largest infrastructure conglomerate now makes its money. Name the series: copper. TimesNow carries the full Q2 figures. Datelined Ahmedabad.

stories.label: Highwaymen: How Cargo Theft Gangs Operate in Costa Rica
stories.summary: Gangs hijacking trucks on Costa Rica's highways use leaked customs data to pick their loads and signal jammers to kill trackers. InSight Crime rode with a Panamanian trucker along the Central American corridor. Lead with the customs-data leak: the theft starts inside the state's own system, which makes it a corruption story as much as a crime story. Datelined San José.

stories.label: Russia plans to establish transport hub on Africa's east coast -- Deputy Foreign Minister
stories.summary: At the Russia-Africa economic forum, Deputy Foreign Minister Sergey Ryabkov said Moscow plans a port and logistics hub on Africa's east coast as part of the International North-South Transport Corridor, and PhosAgro said it will double fertiliser shipments to Africa this year (South Africa, Ethiopia and Mozambique the top buyers). Lead with the hub: it extends a corridor built to route Russian trade around Western sanctions and Suez. Both claims come via Russian state agency TASS and must be attributed. Datelined Moscow.

stories.label: Antarctic sea-ice loss could reshape weather far beyond the pole
stories.summary: A paper published Wednesday documents a sharp rise in salinity in Antarctic surface waters since sea ice began its rapid decline in 2016. Lead with the mechanism: saltier surface water mixes more easily with the warm deep layer, which melts more ice from below, and that feedback can shift ocean circulation and weather far from the pole. Datelined at the research institution.

stories.label: A 60-year search is over: Chemists isolate long-elusive molecules with boron-oxygen triple bonds
stories.summary: Chemists at the University of Würzburg, with computations from Tezpur University in India, report in Nature Chemistry a way to make and isolate stable oxoboranes, molecules with a boron-oxygen triple bond that chemists have chased for over 60 years. Lead with why they were thought too reactive to keep, and what a stable one opens for boron chemistry. Datelined Würzburg.

stories.label: EU-Kommission: Frontex soll zur Abschiebeagentur werden
stories.summary: Two draft laws from the European Commission would turn the border agency Frontex into the EU's central deportation agency, with more staff, more powers and social-media monitoring among its tools; an MEP warns it could become a European version of US immigration police ICE. Lead with the surveillance: what data Frontex would collect on migrants and who checks it. Datelined Brussels.

stories.label: 下中国象棋赢了Jev！扩散智能推出决策模型，判断正确率达95%
stories.summary: Shenzhen startup DiffuSpace, founded by HKU NLP researcher Kong Lingpeng, open-sourced Clover-35B-A3B, a diffusion language model (35B total, 3B active parameters) that it says beats the same-size autoregressive Qwen on six agent and coding benchmarks (SWE-bench Verified 73.6) and generates 680 tokens/s on one GB300. Lead with the architecture bet: diffusion models write blocks of text in parallel instead of one token at a time. Benchmarks are the company's own; say so. Datelined Shenzhen.

stories.label: FBI seizes ‘bulletproof’ hosting site accused of facilitating child abuse, money laundering
stories.summary: The FBI seized the domain of Virtualine, a 'bulletproof' hosting provider accused of hosting child sexual abuse material and serving money launderers and other cybercriminals. Lead with the business model: bulletproof hosts sell immunity from takedown requests, and seizing one knocks out every criminal operation on it at once. Datelined Washington.

stories.label: Lawyers frame India's Kashmir rule as 'settler-colonial', like Israeli occupation of Palestine
stories.summary: The Worldwide Lawyers Association (WOLAS) published a report calling India's rule in Indian-administered Kashmir settler colonialism, and says it will bring universal-jurisdiction cases against Indian officials abroad. Lead with that legal step, not the label: which mechanisms (domicile rules, land transfers, detentions since 2019) the report documents, and which courts could hear such cases. Attribute the claims to WOLAS and give India's position. Datelined Srinagar.

stories.label: Attacker killed outside Belgrade's Israeli embassy - News
stories.summary: A minor attacked a police officer guarding Israel's embassy in Belgrade with a knife and was shot dead. Serbia's outgoing interior minister, Ivica Dačić, called it terrorism. Lead with what is confirmed (the attacker's age, the officer's injuries, who fired), keep the reported ISIS sympathies attributed, and note that it comes days before Serbia's parliamentary election. Datelined Belgrade.

stories.label: Yulan bond debuts in Dubai amid Beijing's yuan-denominated asset push
stories.summary: Bank of China's Dubai branch sold a 2 billion yuan bond in the new 'Yulan' structure, and the order book was five times oversubscribed. Lead with that demand: Gulf money is buying renminbi debt while the Iran war unsettles dollar markets. Explain how the Yulan structure works and why Beijing wants the yuan held in the Gulf, where oil has been priced in dollars. Chart: the yuan. Datelined Dubai.

stories.label: Hundreds stranded as 'cruise for life' operator goes bust over fuel costs
stories.summary: Villa Vie Residences, a US company that sold cabins for passengers to live at sea, ran out of money and left about 200 residents in Sihanoukville, Cambodia, blaming fuel costs. Lead with the stranded people: many sold their homes to buy in. The mechanism is the Iran war's fuel shock reaching a small, thinly capitalised operator. Chart: Brent crude. Datelined Sihanoukville.

stories.label: Revealed: UK relied on £2bn of ‘questionable accounting’ to hit its climate-aid goal
stories.summary: The UK says it has beaten its pledge of £11.6bn in climate aid to developing countries since 2021, but Carbon Brief's analysis of official figures finds that about £2bn of that rests on questionable accounting. Lead with the £2bn and name the items: relabelled existing aid, reclassified spending, investment counted as aid. The countries that lose are the ones the money was promised to. Datelined London.

stories.label: Bangladesh weighs tougher cyber law as AI-generated abuse targets women
stories.summary: Bangladesh's draft cyber law answers a real harm, AI-generated sexual fakes aimed at women, but critics say its broad offences of 'rumour', defamation and disinformation would bring back the censorship of the Digital Security Act. Lead with the trade-off: which clauses protect victims and which give the state room to prosecute speech. Datelined Dhaka.

stories.label: Tencent’s short-drama service reportedly tops 100 million monthly users
stories.summary: Tencent's Lvpaopao short-drama mini-program inside WeChat reached 143 million monthly users in August (QuestMobile, via Jiemian), and weekly users rose 44% in a month to 89.68 million. Lead with the growth, and with the mechanism behind it: free dramas paid for by ads, a growing share of them AI-generated, so production is cheap. This is mainland reporting on China's fastest-growing video format. Datelined Shenzhen.

stories.label: The Freight-App Battle a Chinese “Uber for Trucks” Couldn’t Win
stories.summary: GOGOX, the listed parent of the freight-hailing app Kuaigou Dache, agreed in an October 16 filing to sell its whole mainland China business for one yuan. In 2018 it had spent RMB524m on marketing against RMB453m in revenue. Lead with the one-yuan sale. The mechanism is subsidy wars in platform markets, where the cash-rich leader (Huolala) takes everything and the challenger's spending buys nothing. Datelined Hong Kong.

stories.label: Preprint-centric publishing approach gets major boost
stories.summary: European funders, among them the European Commission, Germany's DFG and France's CNRS, are joining to expand publishing that starts from a preprint and opens peer review to the public, and the Commission rolls out an expanded platform in early November. Lead with what changes for a researcher: publish first, have it reviewed in the open, and pay no fee to a commercial journal. The stake is who controls science's record and its paywalls, including for researchers in the Global South. Datelined Brussels.

stories.label: US costs of Iran war rise to over $47 billion, according to Pentagon estimate
stories.summary: An unpublished Pentagon estimate puts the cost of the Iran war to the US at more than $47 billion, a week before the November 3 midterms in which the war is unpopular. Lead with the figure and the fact that Congress and the public were not shown it. The accountability point is a war being fought without its cost being disclosed. Note the ceasefire it runs alongside, which prediction markets now give 95% odds of holding through October 31. Dateline Washington.

stories.label: US says it killed five people in strike on alleged drug boat
stories.summary: A US strike in the eastern Pacific killed five more people, taking the death toll of the boat-strike campaign to 243 since September 2025. None of the dead were named, charged or tried. Lead with the cumulative toll. The mechanism is a military campaign that legal scholars call extrajudicial killing, run with no public evidence and no court review. Dateline: the eastern Pacific, not Washington.

stories.label: N. Korea Brings Out Howitzers at Inter-Korean Border amid Heightening Tensions
stories.summary: North Korean soldiers were seen inspecting self-propelled guns in Kaepung County, across the river from Gimpo. It is a rare open display of artillery at the inter-Korean border. Lead with what was seen and from where. Then explain the pattern: Pyongyang showing off its guns rather than hiding them, and what that signals to Seoul at a time when North Korean troops and shells have been in the Ukraine war. Dateline Seoul.

stories.label: Jio Platforms opens on BSE over 21% higher with IPO debut at ₹1,357
stories.summary: Jio Platforms rose 21.4% on its first day of trading after India's largest-ever IPO, which puts Mukesh Ambani's telecom and digital arm among the most valuable listed companies in Asia. Lead with the debut gain and the valuation. The structural point is concentration: one conglomerate controls the network that hundreds of millions of Indians use to get online, and it is now on the market. Dateline Mumbai.

stories.label: Indian central bank likely intervenes to support rupee as oil prices weigh, traders say
stories.summary: Traders say the Reserve Bank of India sold dollars on Wednesday to prop up the rupee. India imports most of its oil, and prices kept high by the Iran war and the Hormuz disruption are draining the currency. Lead with the intervention. Then explain the mechanism: Brent crude feeds the import bill, which feeds dollar demand, and the RBI spends its reserves to hold the line. Name Brent crude as the series. Dateline Mumbai.

stories.label: Trump Admin To End Rule Restricting Climate-Warming Emissions From Oil Drilling
stories.summary: Trump is ending the Biden-era rule that limited methane leaks from oil and gas wells, and he says the change will unlock 210 million barrels of oil. That is about 10 days of US consumption. Lead with that ratio: a permanent rise in emissions traded for a few days' supply. The mechanism is that methane traps far more heat than CO2 in its first decades, and the people who bear it are communities near wells in Texas and New Mexico. Dateline Billings.

stories.label: AI worries expose dollar's hot-money problem - AOL
stories.summary: Foreign money that poured into US AI stocks could leave all at once if the boom cracks. That would turn the dollar from a safe haven into something that falls alongside a stock sell-off. Lead with how much of the foreign inflow is chasing AI returns. The mechanism is short-term, return-driven capital: it has no reason to hold dollars once the stocks fall. The Fed decision is due later today. Dateline New York.

stories.label: Coinbase says user funds are safe after vendor exposes customer data
stories.summary: A third-party vendor exposed Coinbase customers' email addresses and phone numbers. Coinbase says funds are safe, but leaked contact details are exactly what crypto phishing and social-engineering scams need. Lead with what leaked and the attack it enables. The structural point is supplier risk: an exchange's security is only as strong as its weakest contractor, the same pattern as the UK police supplier breaches. Dateline San Francisco.

stories.label: Lula da Silva calls Flavio Bolsonaro fleeing Brazil 'shameful' as Trump aide Simon Levy confirms political asylum in US
stories.summary: New development on the runoff arc: the losing candidate who refused to accept Lula's win has left Brazil with his family, the passport-surrender deadline passing as he flew, and Washington says it will issue them visas — a Trump aide calls it political asylum. Lead with the flight and the US decision; the mechanism is a foreign government sheltering a defeated candidate from his own courts, and what it means for the Brazil–US relationship Lula inherits. Agência Pública reported the daughter's school absences that signalled the flight. Datelined Brasília.

stories.label: The UAE Is Secretly Helping Ansarallah Fight Saudi Arabia in Yemen
stories.summary: Drop Site reports the UAE has been covertly sharing targeting assistance with Ansarallah against Saudi-backed forces inside Yemen — the two Gulf partners of the 2015 coalition now on opposite sides. Lead with the reversal and say plainly what the evidence is and who the sources are; set it against the Houthi strike on the Saudi East-West pipeline reported this week. Yemenis pay the cost of a proxy rivalry between their two former 'protectors'. Datelined Sanaa or Aden per the reporting.

stories.label: Killed while livestreaming -- the blogger who exposed Mozambique's chromium pollution road
stories.summary: A Forbidden Stories investigation: Mozambican blogger Mano Shottas was shot dead in late 2024 while livestreaming a protest against chromium ore dumping on the border road to South Africa, and the illegal dumping has continued with no accountability. Lead with the killing on camera and the unanswered question of who fired; the mechanism is a mineral export corridor feeding the global steel chain, where the people breathing the dust are the ones silenced. Datelined Ressano Garcia or the Komati corridor town named in the reporting.

stories.label: Palestinians who fled Gaza for Egypt are being scammed and exploited by fake charities
stories.summary: Palestinians who escaped Gaza to Egypt receive almost no aid and are legally barred from working, which leaves them prey to fake charities and brokers. Lead with the legal limbo — no residency, no right to work — as the mechanism that makes the exploitation possible; name the Egyptian rules and who profits. Datelined Cairo.

stories.label: U.S. Intel Confirms This Is China’s Secret Spaceplane
stories.summary: US intelligence has publicly confirmed the design of China's reusable spaceplane, long flown in secret, and it closely mirrors the US Space Force's X-37B. Lead with the confirmation and what it shows about both powers fielding long-duration, manoeuvrable orbital vehicles with undisclosed missions — the military contest in orbit no treaty governs. Datelined Beijing.

stories.label: Machado's Return Exposes Fault Line in Venezuela's Oil Sector
stories.summary: María Corina Machado's return to Venezuela splits the oil sector: a legitimately elected government would secure property rights, but holders of opaque deals signed under Maduro and Delcy Rodríguez stand to lose them. Lead with who holds those contracts and what Machado has said about honouring them; tie it to Brent crude and the world's largest proven reserves. Datelined Caracas.

stories.label: Italy's Intesa gets ECB authorisation to take over Monte dei Paschi
stories.summary: The ECB has authorised Intesa Sanpaolo, Italy's biggest bank, to take control of Monte dei Paschi — the world's oldest bank, rescued by the state in 2017 — clearing the way for a €32 billion bid. Lead with the size and with who loses: competition in Italian lending and the taxpayers who funded the bailout. Datelined Milan.

stories.label: El déficit con China ya se siente en los mercados de Comayagüela y otros municipios del país
stories.summary: Honduras imported more than $3.1 billion from China in 2025 and exported just $52.9 million (central bank figures), and the gap now shows in the markets: of 78 Chinese-owned shops inspected in Comayagüela, 42-45 had permit irregularities while Honduran traders report falling sales and closures. Lead with the 60-to-1 trade ratio; the mechanism is what Honduras got when it switched recognition from Taiwan to Beijing in 2023. Datelined Tegucigalpa.

stories.label: Govt raises currency transaction report threshold to Rs3m
stories.summary: Pakistan has raised by 50% the cash-transaction threshold at which banks must file reports to the State Bank's Financial Monitoring Unit, from Rs2 million to Rs3 million, under the Anti-Money Laundering Act. Lead with what falls out of scrutiny and why now (inflation eroding the old figure versus FATF obligations Pakistan exited the grey list on). Accountability angle: fewer reports on cash in a cash-heavy economy. Datelined Islamabad.

stories.label: Code-execution flaw in UEFI firmware threatens most servers on planet Earth
stories.summary: A critical code-execution flaw in EDK2, the open-source UEFI firmware nearly every server vendor builds on, lets attackers run code early in boot — before the operating system and below most defences. Lead with the reach (most of the world's data centres) and the mechanism: one shared firmware base means one bug ships through every vendor, and patching firmware is slow. Name the trigger (network boot path) and whether exploitation is seen.

stories.label: "No human at the helm": Delaware plan would let AI agents run entire businesses
stories.summary: Delaware, where most large US companies are incorporated, is weighing a rule letting companies be operated entirely by AI agents; Rep. James Comer warns it would let human owners evade liability for reckless AI actions. Lead with the liability gap — who is answerable when no human is at the helm — and why Delaware's choice sets the default for corporate law. Datelined Dover.

stories.label: Apple unveils MacBook Pro with up to 24 hours of battery life
stories.summary: Apple launched M6-based MacBook Pro (from $1,999) and iMac (from $1,499). Skip the spec sheet; lead with the chip — what M6 changes for on-device AI and graphics, who fabricates it, and how Apple's in-house silicon compares with the Intel/AMD/Qualcomm field. Datelined Cupertino.

stories.label: Warning Signals: Venezuela and the Risk of AI-Powered Chinese Digital Authoritarianism
stories.summary: An ASPI report warns Venezuela could plug Chinese AI into its existing surveillance stack (the ZTE-built 'carnet de la patria' ID system, camera networks), expanding state digital control. Lead with the concrete systems already in place and which Chinese vendors supply them; the reader should see the surveillance infrastructure any new government inherits. Note ASPI's funding and perspective. Datelined Caracas.

stories.label: Double debris disk orbiting a dead star hints at our solar system's future
stories.summary: ESO's Very Large Telescope found a white dwarf ringed by a double debris disk split by a clear gap, apparently sculpted by two surviving planetary bodies, one perhaps Pluto-sized. Lead with the survivors: worlds that outlived their star's death, a preview of what remains of our solar system in about 5 billion years. Name the star, the distance and the journal.

stories.label: Lina Attalah in custody after court issues LE3 mn fine, orders Mada Masr’s closure
stories.summary: An Egyptian court handed Mada Masr editor Lina Attalah the maximum penalty, a LE3 million fine, and ordered the closure of Egypt's last major independent newsroom; she is being held in custody at the courthouse. Lead with the closure order: the state is not just punishing a journalist but shutting the outlet itself. Name the court, the charges and the law used, and place it in Sisi's record of blocking and prosecuting independent media. Datelined Cairo.

stories.label: 2 men charged with national security offenses in suspected U.K. air base plot
stories.summary: Two British nationals were charged under the National Security Act over a suspected plot against RAF Fairford, the base that hosts the US bombers flown in the Iran war; one is charged with assisting Iran's intelligence service. Lead with the base and why it matters: the war's front has reached the British countryside through a launch site for strikes on Iran. Report the charges exactly as the Crown Prosecution Service set them out; these are allegations, not findings. Datelined London.

stories.label: Lavrov warns Russia-Ukraine conflict could escalate - ProtoThema English
stories.summary: New since the Putin–Stubb–Støre call (covered this morning): Lavrov said the war will continue and likely escalate, while calling the new Russian–American diesel deal a 'purely business arrangement with no additional conditions'. Lead with that contradiction: Moscow and Washington are trading fuel while Russia's foreign minister rules out an end to the war. Explain what the diesel deal covers and who it relieves; attribute Lavrov's claims to him. Datelined Moscow.

stories.label: Садыр Жапаров признал, что Алексей Ширшов стоит за майнингом на Камбар-Ате 2. «Клооп» писал об этом еще три года назад
stories.summary: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov publicly admitted that Alexei Shirshov, architect of the Bakiyev-era energy corruption schemes, is behind the crypto mining at the Kambar-Ata 2 state hydropower plant, confirming what Kloop reported three years ago; in the same tour he praised Shirshov and mocked his former partner Maxim Bakiyev. Lead with the admission: a head of state vouching for a man tied to the schemes that toppled a president, while the country's hydropower feeds a private mining operation in a nation with winter power shortages. Datelined Bishkek.

stories.label: Iran threatens South Korean shipping group over Hormuz transits
stories.summary: Iran threatened South Korean shipowner Sinokor with 'legal action' for repeated 'crossing violations' of the transit rules Tehran has imposed on the Strait of Hormuz, rules it has so far enforced only by military force. Lead with the shift: Iran is now treating the strait as its own regulated waterway and naming individual companies. Explain what the rules demand, how many Sinokor vessels crossed, and what it means for insurers and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, and for Brent crude, while ceasefire talks continue. Datelined Tehran.

stories.label: Brazil's real sinks after Lula's re-election victory
stories.summary: New since the 10-26 market-slump story: CoinDesk reports Brazilian companies moved cash into dollar stablecoins on election day to dodge a currency crash, and the Brazilian real is now down about 6.2% against the dollar in a week. Lead with the stablecoin flight: firms used crypto rails to exit the real faster than the banking system allows. Name the Brazilian real, what investors fear in Lula's fiscal plans, and who pays for a weaker currency: importers and households facing dearer fuel and food. Datelined São Paulo.

stories.label: ANALYSIS: Nigeria's first methane disclosure raises questions over repeated figures, missing data
stories.summary: Nigeria's first company-level greenhouse gas disclosure contains repeated emissions figures, incomplete methane reporting and an inconsistent list of companies that filed. Lead with the repeated figures: the baseline Nigeria will be judged against, and that oil companies' flaring is measured by, may not be real data. Name the regulator, which operators filed and which did not, and why methane matters in the Niger Delta, where flaring and leaks land on communities. Datelined Abuja.

stories.label: Govt to end slab system punishing consumers crossing 200-unit threshold
stories.summary: Pakistan's power minister Awais Leghari told the Senate the government will scrap the electricity slab rule under which a household using 201 units instead of 200 loses its protected tariff for months, and move to targeted subsidies. Lead with the one-unit cliff and what it costs a family who crosses it; then the mechanism: who decides who is 'deserving', and whether the IMF programme drives the change. Datelined Islamabad.

stories.label: Fish scarcity, tar balls, and stranded dolphins: The hidden costs of offshore platforms in Cameroon waters
stories.summary: Offshore oil and gas platforms off Kribi pay into Cameroon's budget while coastal fishers report vanishing catches, tar balls on beaches and stranded dolphins, and Indigenous coastal communities bear the cost. Lead with the fishers: who gets the oil revenue and who loses a livelihood. Name the operators and the regulator, and check the budget figure (FCFA 774.51 billion is about $1.3 billion, not $1.3 million as the summary says). Datelined Kribi.

stories.label: DeepMind's Genie 4 world model adds audio and more realistic people to simulations
stories.summary: Google DeepMind's Genie 4 generates interactive worlds with sound and more realistic people, and is rolling out to developers and AI Ultra subscribers. Lead with what is new over Genie 3, which sent gaming stocks down last year: the move from demo to product. The structural why: world models are where labs now train agents and robots, and access is going first to paying subscribers. Datelined London.

stories.label: Hackers repeatedly breached suppliers holding UK police data, watchdog finds
stories.summary: His Majesty's Inspectorate of Constabulary found that British police data was breached several times this decade through third-party IT suppliers. Lead with the count and what was exposed: the weak point is not the forces but the contractors they hand data to. Name the suppliers if the report does, and what the inspectorate recommends. Datelined London.

stories.label: Account-Sperren auf Instagram und Facebook: Metas Willkür unterworfen
stories.summary: Meta is suspending Instagram and Facebook accounts of organisations and individuals in Germany without a clear reason, and the bans fall disproportionately on queer and progressive accounts, which lose reach overnight. Lead with a named case and what it cost; the mechanism is automated moderation with no working appeal, and the accountability question is whether the EU's Digital Services Act, which requires a statement of reasons, is being enforced. Datelined Berlin.

stories.label: Guest post: Greenland ice sheet shrinks for 30th year in a row
stories.summary: Greenland's ice sheet lost more ice than it gained for the 30th consecutive year, according to the annual mass-balance assessment. Lead with the 12-month loss in gigatonnes and its contribution to sea level; then the mechanism (surface melt versus glacier calving) and who is exposed: low-lying coasts from Bangladesh to the Nile Delta. Datelined Nuuk.

stories.label: General-purpose AI as a source of mental health support amongst 24,000 adolescents in England - npj Mental Health Research
stories.summary: A survey of 24,000 adolescents in England measured how many turn to general-purpose AI chatbots for mental health support. Lead with the share and who is most likely to use them (age, gender, those already struggling); the structural point is that a teenager's first source of help is now an unregulated product built for something else. Report the study's limits as it states them. Datelined London.
